To elaborate, EPA claims states have no authority to certify in areas of exclusive federal jurisdiction, thus vesting EPA with sole 401 certification authority within Yellowstone National Park. See 33 U.S.C. § 1341(a)(1). However, Wyoming has issued 401 certifications in Yellowstone National Park since 1973. So to the extent EPA now characterizes the Park as an area of exclusive federal jurisdiction, neither the facts nor the law has changed - only EPA's interpretation. EPA erroneously treats the word "authority" as synonymous with the word "jurisdiction." The statute already uses the word "jurisdiction," indicating that Congress' choice to use the word "authority" should be treated differently. Justification: Pursuant to 13 CFR § 125.8(e) and 13 CFR § 124.513, the purpose of the Mentor-Protégé program is to enhance the capabilities of the Protégé and ensure they perform a "meaningful" role in the procurement. Currently, the MAPS scoring architecture allows a JV to achieve a maximum score by leveraging only the QPs and CPARS of a Large Business Mentor or a multi-billion dollar ANC parent affiliate. This allows "Paper JVs" to outscore independent Small Businesses (under $15M) that are performing 100% of their own work, without the Protégé proving any individual technical competence. Requiring the Small Business partner to provide at least one QP of their own ensures a level playing field and confirms that the Government is awarding contracts to teams where the Small Business has a proven, foundational role in mission success. This prevents the "Small Business" set-aside from being dominated by large-business expe
